theme: Blessed is the man, the two ways behind the Sermon
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 1. This short psalm is the doorway to the whole Psalter, and its two paths sit right behind the Sermon on the Mount. Read it aloud and compare the tree with the chaff.
settingTheScene: Psalm 1 has no title and no author, and it opens the book of Psalms by setting two ways of life side by side. After reading Jesus’ Sermon, with its two gates, two trees, and two foundations, you can hear that Jesus was drawing on this psalm. It is a wisdom poem that asks the reader to choose.
observation: “Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked” (v. 1).
“Nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of scoffers” (v. 1).
“But his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night” (v. 2).
“He is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in its season” (v. 3).
“In all that he does, he prospers” (v. 3).
“The wicked are not so, but are like chaff that the wind drives away” (v. 4).
“For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish” (v. 6).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with a progression: walking, standing, sitting. The person who drifts from listening to the wicked, to lingering with sinners, to settling in with scoffers is on a slide. The blessed person turns away from this and finds his delight in God’s law, his instruction, and thinks about it all the time.

The picture of the tree is lovely. It is planted, not wild, so someone has put it where the water is. Its roots go down to the stream, and so it bears fruit in season and its leaf does not wither. A person who is rooted in God’s word is not immune to hardship, but he has resources the world does not see.

The wicked are like chaff, the light husk of the grain that blows away when the wheat is threshed. They have no weight and no roots. “The wicked will not stand in the judgment.” The psalm ends with the contrast: the LORD knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the wicked will perish. To be known by the LORD is the ultimate security.

Read after Matthew 5 to 7, the psalm gets sharper. Who is the truly blessed man who perfectly delights in the law and never walks with sinners? Jesus. He is the true tree planted by the water, and he is the one who gives his Spirit so that others may be rooted in him. The Beatitudes echo this psalm’s first word: “Blessed.” The Sermon on the Mount is the same invitation to choose the path of life.
connection: Jeremiah 17:7-8 uses the same tree image for the one who trusts in the LORD. John 15:5 says, “I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit.” Matthew 7:24-27 is Jesus’ version of the two ways. Joshua 1:8 commands meditating on the book of the law day and night. Colossians 2:6-7 says to be rooted and built up in him. Revelation 22:2 shows the tree of life by the river.
application:
Take five minutes today to meditate on one verse, not just read it. Turn it over and ask what it means.

Ask who or what is shaping your “counsel” right now: the voices you listen to and the company you keep.

Memorize verses 1 to 3 as a picture of the life you want.
prayerPrompts: Tell God you want to be a tree planted by streams of water.
Ask him to keep you from the counsel of the wicked.
Thank him that he knows your way.
